messages:
Anya: quick flag 1: found several outdated function/tool-calling snippets in the docs. some links 404 and a few examples still show function_call payloads. can we triage?

Kelsey: I can run linkcheck and start fixes. Do you have the grep output?

Anya: put it in the issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/980 - most hits under /docs/guides/tool-calling/ and /docs/reference/structured-output/.

Kelsey: ok creating branch docs/links/toolcall-fix-kc. I'll redirect broken slugs to a legacy folder where necessary.

Matt: for snippet changes: prefer demonstrating tools as first-class objects. example diff i suggest:```py
# before
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
  model="x",
  function_call={"name": "get_price"},
)
# after
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
  model="x",
  tools=[get_price],
)
```
Also add a tiny note about providing a JSON schema for tool args and how parser fallbacks behave.

Sri: on structured-output: replace the older "top-level array" examples with a compact envelope pattern and show an explicit schema. also call out that unions-of-arrays are brittle for parsers.

Kelsey: CI linkcheck snippet from pipeline:
```
LinkChecker: 404 on /examples/tool-old.md (ref in /docs/guides/tool-calling/index.md)
```
I'll patch that redirect and update internal links.

DocsBot: automated: linkcheck discovered 9 broken links this run. full report: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/12345

Anya: scope: do link fixes in PR1 (safe). PR2 for snippet migrations + a 3-line migration note in /docs/migration.md that directs readers to the compact examples and SDK changes.

Kelsey: opened PR1: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4601 - redirects and link fixes. tagging @Matt @Sri.

Matt: will review PR1 tomorrow. for PR2 i can draft the before/after code snippets in python and ts and a small paragraph on parser fallback ordering.

Sri: i'll write the guardrails blurb: prefer explicit property types; require critical keys at top-level; example showing parser fallback order (schema > compact-envelope > heuristics).

Kelsey: adding a compact envelope sample to be added under /docs/reference/structured-output/compact-envelopes.md. draft snippet:
```json
{
  "envelope": {
    "tool_call": {"name": "summarize", "args": {"text": "..."}},
    "output_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["summary"]}
  }
}
```
This will be the canonical example and we'll point migration.md to it.

Matt: small note: the SDK snippets should show import patterns and how to register tool call handlers in both py and ts. i'll include a tiny ts example:```ts
// new
const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'x', tools: [summarize] })
```

Kelsey: PR1 merged :tada: - redirects in place. moving on to PR2 for snippets. opened PR2: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4610

Matt: reviewed PR2, left a minor wording nit on the migration note. also suggested adding a line about backwards compatibility for older SDKs.

Sri: reviewed and approved, added guardrails expansion for arrays/unions.

Kelsey: addressed nits, updated python/ts snippets, added migration note to /docs/migration.md (3 lines). preview built: https://deploy-preview.redwood-inference.io/preview/4610

DocsBot: automated: docs preview successful. pipeline: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/preview/4610

Kelsey: merged PR2. If folks find more old examples ping me and i'll spin follow-ups. thanks! :thumbsup:
